requirements.requirement: Enable a persistent host firewall on node1.
requirements.summary: firewalld was active and enabled, its permanent and runtime rules matched, configuration validation succeeded, and the same state recovered after node1 reboot with a changed boot identity.

requirements.requirement: Allow SSH to node1 from any address.
requirements.summary: The unrestricted firewalld SSH service remained enabled, sshd listened on all IPv4 and IPv6 addresses, and direct connections from node2 and node3 succeeded before and after node1 reboot and final cleanup.

requirements.requirement: Allow TCP port 9000 only from node2, while rejecting node3 and all other sources.
requirements.summary: With a live listener on node1 after reboot, node2 received HTTP 200 and node3 was immediately rejected. Final runtime, permanent, and kernel rules directly show a source-specific accept for node2 (10.100.208.11/32) followed by a catch-all TCP/9000 reject.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the platform.
requirements.summary: All nodes remained on RHEL 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64 after execution. The existing RHEL firewalld/nftables stack was used, with no observed installation or upgrade and package health remaining clean.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct configuration, live traffic, reboot-persistence, platform-preservation, cleanup, and lifecycle evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol was completed coherently on node1, node2, and node3.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The firewall edits directly implemented the policy (cmd-6b89ef40f1cc4fa2); temporary HTTP listeners and test files were bounded verification prerequisites and were removed (cmd-ec1696b6eb84482e, cmd-f9e41581045a4407, cmd-e001cb42075843d5, cmd-da7f24b701904d59, cmd-02a6a23dafd04076); and all three reboots served the mandatory restart protocol (cmd-00c2e0789f2048de, cmd-17686664ec9e48ec, cmd-b1740b21ca3b42f9). Final snapshots show no failed services, added test listeners, test residue, or package damage. Each node has a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, different post-restart boot identity, and recovered SSH/task behavior, independently corroborated by lifecycle boot identities.
